name: Calculating the Average of Input Integers
description: Construct a program that reads a series of integers from the user, sums them up, and calculates their average. The user enters 0 to indicate the end of the input.
code:
#Step 1: Assign initial values to the variables which we need for this program
total = 0
count = 0
#Step 2: Read the first integer that the user enters
text = input("Enter an integer (0 to quit): ")
num = int(text)
#Step 3: Process the integer that the user has entered, then receive and process the next integers as long as the user enters a non-zero integer; otherwise stop
while num != 0 :
    count += 1
    total += num
    print("The sum so far is", total, ", count =", count)
    text = input("Enter an integer (0 to quit): ")
    num = int(text)
#Step 4: Calculate and print the average of the integers entered by the user
if count == 0 :
    print("No integers were entered.")
else :
    average = total / count
print("The average is:", average)

comments.content: We need variable total to maintain a running total, which means the sum of the integers that the user enters.
We need variable count to count how many integers the user enters. This is required for calculating the average of the integers that the user enters.

We need to read and process the input value that the user enters. To read the input value from the user, we need to use the input() function. This statement prompts the user to enter an integer, then reads the text entered by the user and places it in the variable text. The value that will be stored in variable text is a string.
We need to convert the input text to its integer representation. For this purpose, we use the conversion function int().

Note that the conversion to integer can only be done if the string actually presents a number. If the input number is a float, the int() function cuts off the fractional part of the floating-point number to create an integer.

We need to process the integer that the user has entered and repeat receiving and processing the integers from the user as long as the user enters an integer that is different from 0. Therefore, we need to use a loop structure. Since we don't know ahead of time how many times the loop will be repeated, we need to use a while loop. The condition in the while loop tests whether the body of the loop should be repeated, so it should test whether the input integer is different from 0.
The body of the while loop is repeated as long as the user enters an integer that is different from 0. The loop terminates when the loop condition evaluates to False, that is when the user enters 0.

We have to count the number of integers that are entered because we need it for calculating the average. Therefore, each time that the user enters an integer, we need to increment the number of integers that user has entered by 1. Note that if the user enters 0, it will not be counted.

The += operator adds the value on the right-hand side of the assignment operator (i.e., 1) to the current value of the variable on the left-hand side (i.e., value of variable count) and the result is stored in the variable count. Thus, this statement is equivalent to the statement count = count + 1.
We need to add the integer that the user has entered to the running total. So, each time that the user enters an integer, that integer needs to be added to and stored back into total.

The += operator adds the value on the right-hand side of the assignment operator (i.e., value of variable num) to the current value of the variable on the left-hand side (i.e., value of variable total) and the result is stored in the variable total. Thus, this statement is equivalent to the statement total = total + num.

Each time the body of the while loop is repeated, the sum and the number of the integers that the user has entered will be printed to the default standard output stream. We do this to see how sum and count are updated after each repeat of the loop.
The printed text shows the arguments of the print function separated by the default delimiter (i.e., single space character) and followed by the end-of-line character at the end.

We need to read and process the next integer value that the user enters. To read the input value from the user, we need to use the input() function. This statement prompts the user to enter the next integer, then reads the text entered by the user and places it in the variable text. The value that will be stored in variable text is a string.
We need to convert the input text to its integer representation. For this purpose, we use the conversion function int().

Note that the conversion to integer can only be done if the string actually presents a number. If the input number is a float, the int() function cuts off the fractional part of the floating-point number to create an integer.

We need the if statement at the end of the program to avoid a divide-by-zero error. This occurs if the user immediately enters zero before entering any other integers.

To determine if the divide-by-zero error would occur, we need to test if the number of integers entered by the user is equal to zero.
If the number of integers that the user has entered is equal to zero, then the body of this if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this if statement is skipped.
This statement prints to the default standard output stream that no integers were entered. This text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.

If the above if test fails (i.e., when the number of integers the the user has entered is different from zero), we could calculate the average by dividing the sum by the number of integers entered by the user.

We need to calculate the average by dividing the sum of the integers by the number of the integers that the user entered. Note that since we want to keep the fractional part of the division result, we need to use the real division by using / operator.

This statement prints to the default standard output stream the text "The average is:" and the value of variable average.
The printed text shows the arguments of the print function separated by the default delimiter (i.e., single space character) and followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
